subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards keep the CardKit full-content contract only, or add a documented opt-in append/delta mode for deployments that prove full-content updates are too slow?
rationale: The reported regression is real enough to keep open, but the obvious config-mode fix conflicts with the earlier truncation fix and the linked coalescing PR is now disputed by fresh live repro evidence.

options.title: Require Proof, Then Add Opt-In Mode
options.body: Recommended: require redacted live Feishu/Gateway timing and payload proof, then add an explicit append/delta mode only if it preserves full-content as the default and documents the truncation tradeoff.

options.title: Keep Full-Content Only
options.body: Reject append mode and continue pursuing a full-content-compatible latency fix such as safer batching, fewer final flushes, or upstream CardKit guidance.

options.title: Accept Coalescing Candidate
options.body: Proceed with the linked coalescing pull request only if maintainers decide its source-level reduction is enough despite the latest live comment saying it did not fix the tail.

recommendation.title: Require Proof, Then Add Opt-In Mode
recommendation.body: Recommended: require redacted live Feishu/Gateway timing and payload proof, then add an explicit append/delta mode only if it preserves full-content as the default and documents the truncation tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the declared community owner for the Feishu/Lark plugin package, and the decision is specific to that channel's CardKit behavior.
